clue.text: Big exhibition attracting inevitable publicity

parts.note: an expo is a large trade or world exhibition
something inevitable is sure to happen

explanation.surface: A huge show draws a burst of press attention that could not be avoided.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage that puts someone in the public eye is called exposure.

clue.text: English politician with a passion for power

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: An English member of parliament is passionate about power.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm under one supreme authority, a seat of power and dominion.

clue.text: Current value put on one's capital

indicators.note: put on means placed above in a down answer, so the value word sits on top

parts.note: par is the standard or normal value of something
one's read as one is gives I and IS

explanation.surface: A present-day valuation is placed on someone's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it is a capital city; 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Car, second time after time, finally first

indicators.note: finally places the word for first at the end of the build

parts.note: oft means often, time after time
top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: A car keeps coming second, but at last comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft top is a convertible car whose roof is folding fabric.

clue.text: Exciting ride in vessel overwhelmed by large wave

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means lying beneath, so in this down answer the vessel goes under the wave

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave
a coaster is a small ship trading along the coast

explanation.surface: A thrilling trip on a boat swamped by a huge wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground ride on a steep, twisting track of rising and plunging cars.

clue.text: Another messenger? That covers him

explanation.surface: A riddle about a go-between and what he wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual messenger of the gods in crosswords is the Roman Mercury, hence 'Another' for his Greek counterpart; the second reading is the Paris fashion house whose ties and scarves dress a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god who carried messages for Zeus, and the Paris luxury label famous for silk ties and clothing that cover a wearer.

clue.text: Expunged a handful of notes

parts.note: a handful of musical notes, each named by a letter from A to G
a handful of musical notes, each named by a letter from A to G
a handful of musical notes, each named by a letter from A to G
a handful of musical notes, each named by a letter from A to G
a handful of musical notes, each named by a letter from A to G
a handful of musical notes, each named by a letter from A to G
a handful of musical notes, each named by a letter from A to G

explanation.surface: Erased with just a few notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the answer is a note of the musical scale, A to G, so the seven notes spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to rub out or obliterate, so effaced means wiped out.

clue.text: Lying people start to deceive a whole town

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of deceive is taken

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Liars set out to deceive an entire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is untruthfulness, the habit of telling lies.

clue.text: Costliest production losing a little time: the longest day

indicators.note: production means making something new, so the remaining letters are rearranged
losing means a letter is taken away from costliest before the mix

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The priciest show cuts a few minutes on midsummer day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops one T from COSTLIEST, and 'production' rearranges the COSLIEST left.
explanation.definitionFit: The summer solstice falls in late June and is the day with most daylight in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Shares wine with pages

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
a folio is a leaf or page of a book

explanation.surface: Someone splits a bottle of wine while reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor's holding of stocks and shares is their portfolio.

clue.text: Last swallow departing?

parts.note: not a bird flying south but the final drink a guest gulps before leaving the pub or party

explanation.definitionFit: A final drink taken just before setting off home is a traditional parting tipple.

clue.text: Last decoration on roof I removed

indicators.note: removed says the letter I named just before it is taken out of the ornament word

parts.note: a finial is an ornament topping a roof gable or spire

explanation.surface: The last ornament is taken off the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes at the very end, like the closing match of a cup, is the final one.

clue.text: You have to steer deviously to find favour

indicators.note: deviously means by a winding, indirect route, so the letters of to and steer are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip on currying favour: steer things in a roundabout way.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon badge worn as a token of support, the same thing as a ribbon rosette.

clue.text: Liking to appear penniless arriving at entrance

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, so the coin's abbreviation P is dropped from the liking word

parts.note: a penchant is a liking or fondness

explanation.surface: Someone with a taste for something turns up at the door broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to put under a spell; P is the abbreviation for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or bewitch them, as a charm does.

clue.text: Hard copy about an orchid translated by Moliere's eponym

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: about here means turned around and jumbled, so the letters of copy are mixed
translated means put into another form, so the letters of an orchid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A printout about a flower is translated by a French playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Moliere's play Le Malade imaginaire is known in English as The Imaginary Invalid, its title figure being a man convinced he is ill.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Moliere's last comedy is an anxious man forever imagining illnesses.

clue.text: Jug is meant to stand up

definitions.meaning: a jug is meant to contain liquid without leaking
to stand up is to be sound and convincing, as an argument does

explanation.surface: A jug is supposed to stay upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug's job is to contain liquid, and an argument that is sound survives scrutiny; both senses share the idiom.

clue.text: Let's chat about personal property

indicators.note: about means turned around and rearranged, so the letters of let's chat are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An invitation to discuss someone's belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattels are movable possessions, as distinct from land or buildings.

clue.text: Showing little enthusiasm, so nineteen would be beaten

parts.note: the answer as an instruction: treat the 19-down word this way, losing half its central double N, and it becomes a word for beaten

explanation.surface: A lacklustre effort, so number nineteen would lose.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19-down answer has NN at its heart; drop half of it and CANED, meaning thrashed or beaten, is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without real commitment or energy is doing it halfheartedly.

clue.text: Nasty mould discovered under house — tough!

indicators.note: under means the jumbled letters come beneath the house letters in this down answer
nasty means unpleasant or twisted, so the letters of mould are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foul mould found below the house: tough luck!
explanation.walkthrough: 'tough' looks like an exclamation of sympathy, but it is a noun, a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a violent street criminal, the same as a thug or gangster.

clue.text: See twenty-two's heart stop — heart is removed

parts.note: the middle three letters of the 22-down answer, a word for a fool

indicators.note: heart is removed means the middle letter of the stop word is taken out

parts.note: to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: A heart-stopping moment for a cardiac patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a bishop's see, the district under a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the area under his authority, the same as his diocese.

clue.text: A lot of beer is drunk

definitions.meaning: much beer is sold sealed in tins

explanation.surface: Plenty of beer gets drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer sealed in tins is sold this way, and British slang uses the same word for tipsy.

clue.text: Tug from child grabbing women's scarf

indicators.note: grabbing means the child word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
W is the abbreviation for women
a boa is a long feathery scarf

explanation.surface: A toddler snatches a woman's scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful vessel for pulling ships, also called a towboat.

clue.text: Time to get hold of aural pornography

indicators.note: to get hold of means the time word grips the other letters within it

parts.note: an era is a period of time
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: It is time to tackle audio smut.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic writing or pictures intended to arouse are a milder term for pornography.

clue.text: Ignoramus's ignorance doesn't irritate ordinary teachers, only heads

indicators.note: only heads means just the first letter of each of the five words is used

explanation.surface: A dunce's ignorance doesn't bother ordinary teachers, only head teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' looks like head teachers, but it means the first letters of the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, a fool.

clue.text: Former partner's left — about to celebrate

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the partner and left letters go round the word to

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An ex has walked out and someone is about to party.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, to laud or glorify.

clue.text: Once African island visited by Scot

indicators.note: visited by means the island is joined by the Scot coming after it

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Greek island gets a visit from a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodesia was the former name of the country now called Zimbabwe, hence 'Once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the former southern African state now Zimbabwe was a Rhodesian.

clue.text: Rugby players quietly indulge in theft

parts.note: the scrum is the pack of forwards in rugby
P is piano, the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: Rugby forwards are caught pilfering on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: To scrump is British slang for stealing fruit, especially apples, from an orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumping is a British word for petty thieving, typically apples from someone's tree.

clue.text: Mentioned bill and Edward

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A bill and a man named Edward came up in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is a formal way of saying to refer to it.
